long_biography.plain_text:
Delaportas spent school holidays in Meadway Shipping & Trading, founded by his father Dionysis in 1988, then entered the business professionally in the early 2000s. As commercial and chartering director, he opened operating offices in Singapore and Dubai and pushed the business beyond conventional vessel ownership into cargo contracts and chartered tonnage. He also oversaw the move into larger Handymax ships and developed relationships with Japanese yards and financial partners.

Following his father's death and a 2021 division of the family enterprise, Delaportas led the branch later renamed DryDel. He broadened its network to the Americas, renewed the owned fleet with fuel-efficient Japanese bulkers and entered Capesize construction. The company now combines owned ships, long- and short-term chartered vessels, and millions of tonnes of third-party cargo. That operating model keeps its commercial exposure close to physical freight flows.

uncertainties: Identity is resolved at 100. Companies House supplies the formal Konstantinos Delaportas name, May 1977 birth month and year, Greek residence, controlling ownership and exact DryDel address. DryDel and trade sources use Costas, Greek reporting uses Kostas, and Burgess directly names Costas Delaportas as Maestro's owner. No similarly named shipping figure matches this complete set of anchors.

Costas and Kostas are professional and transliterated short forms of Konstantinos in this record. The corporate register and Slide2Open URL use Konstantinos, while all current company, conference and yacht sources use Costas. The established professional first_name is retained rather than replaced by the legal form, and Konstantinos is recorded only as an identity variant.

The surname appears as Delaportas in authoritative and current professional sources. Some TradeWinds results use Dellaportas, and Companies House spells the father's surname Dellaportas while spelling Konstantinos's name Delaportas. These are source variants, not separate identities, and no surname change is proposed.

The authoritative birth day is 12 May 1977; Companies House independently confirms only May 1977. The exact company, control, address, nationality and residence make the partial-date corroboration decisive without using the day as an externally verified proposal.

Dionysios Delaportas founded the predecessor company in 1988. Mononews later calls Costas founder of his branch while BOAT International describes his creation of the independent DryDel company after the family succession. Founder is therefore not used for the principal wealth relationship; Operator better preserves the distinction between founding the original platform and reorganising its successor branch.

Companies House records the father's control ceasing and Konstantinos acquiring at least 75% control in July 2019, the year independent reporting says Dionysios died. The record strongly supports inheritance, but it does not publish the probate instrument, exact estate allocation or private terms of the later brother-company division.

Inherited and expanded is used because Delaportas received control of a family-founded core platform and then made a documented material contribution to its scale. He had already built the operator business and Asian and Middle Eastern offices before succession, then enlarged the fleet, orderbook, cargo programme and American footprint after becoming chief executive.

George Delaportas controls the separate Meadway Bulkers business after the 2021 division. His vessels, offices, transactions and management record are excluded from Costas's classifications and biographies unless a source explicitly attributes an activity to DryDel or Costas.

Dry-bulk shipping and Ship chartering are the minimum-useful approved tags. The former captures the principal operating sector; the latter captures a separately documented, repeated cargo-and-chartered-tonnage business model. Generic shipping and prospective tanker activity do not add a supported taxonomy distinction.

The input biography states that Delaportas 'becomes' a member of the Institute of Chartered Shipbrokers and devotes much of its limited space to education. A 51-word replacement corrects the grammar and centres the current wealth mechanism; the longer dossier biography preserves formative education and career context separately.

The existing display_name duplicates the separately stored Mr title. Current company, conference, trade and yacht sources consistently use Costas Delaportas without the honorific, so a display-name correction is proposed while retaining the existing title field.

The official company website is proposed as Company Website. The existing LinkedIn profile is corroborated by DryDel affiliation, Athens geography and shipping education, but is not duplicated as a proposal. No collision-safe personal Instagram or personal website was found.

No reliable public source establishes a place of birth or secondary nationality. Greek residence is proposed from the official corporate register; the broader Athens and Voula business geography alone is not used to infer birthplace.

Burgess and BOAT International directly establish the Maestro relationship, while SuperYacht Times confirms the exact 41.1-metre, 351-GT Mondomarine vessel. Maestro, all earlier yachts, refit spending, charter activity, design detail and transaction timing are excluded from the biographies.
